content.english: I shall sing to the One awesome in praises,

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!
The one who created varied forms in His universe
Chose Israel among all the others.
Therefore, we shall sing joyous songs
For Him; we shall awaken with our praise.

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!
He desired and sanctified the seventh day for Himself.
He called it “the Sabbath,” my King and my Shepherd.

content.hebrew: בּוֹ יוֹם אֲנִי אֶשְׁכַּח : נוֹדִי וְנוֹעִי
content.transliteration: Bo yom ani eshkaḥ : nodi veno‘i
content.english: On that day, I shall forget all my wanderings

content.hebrew: אַקְדִּישׁ בְּשִֹמְחָה רַב : תּוֹךְ כָּל קְהִלּוֹת:
content.transliteration: Aḳdish besimḥa rav : toch kol ḳehillot.
content.english: And joyously hallow the One great among all congregations.

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!
Sanctify yourselves today, O descendants of the righteous!
Small and great alike, children and parents!
All your sorrows and confusions, O pure and untainted ones—

content.hebrew: עִזְבוּ וְשַׁבְּחוּ צוּר : עִם קוֹל הֲמוּלּוֹת:
content.english: Leave them behind and praise the Rock with festive sound!

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!
Turn away and flee from the delights of the body,
Instead, go and chase after intellectual delights!

content.hebrew: הַיּוֹם בְּנֵי אֵל חַי : חוּשׁוּ וְהִלְכוּ
content.transliteration: Hayyom bené el ḥai : ḥushu vehilchu
content.english: Today, O children of the living God, go in haste

content.hebrew: בֵּית אֵל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל : עִם רוֹב תְּפִלּוֹת:
content.english: To God’s house and pray a host of prayers.

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!
He will soon destroy the plunderers and thugs,
The Rock will bring upon them indignation and wrath.
If you observe the Sabbath without transgression,
You will soon be released from darkness.

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!
The one who remembers and redeems will remember His covenant
And restore the people of His inheritance upon their mound.
The Rock will truly fulfill His word:
I shall return, and the House of Habitation will be rebuilt!

content.hebrew: אֵל חַי : אֵל חַי וְהַקַּיָּם : עוֹשֶֹה גְדוֹלוֹת:
content.transliteration: El ḥai, el ḥai vehaḳḳayyam :‘osé ḡedolot.
content.english: The Living God / the Living and Abiding God who performs great deeds!

introduction:
Introduction

אשיר בשירה אל נורא תהלות, Ashir Beshira El Nora Tehillot

Introduction:  This poem for the Sabbath discusses God as the Creator of the Universe, who chose Israel. The Sabbath must be hallowed with joy; studying is ideal on the Sabbath; the keepers of the Sabbath will be released from the darkness of exile. The poem ends with the hope for God’s promise to restore His nation to its rightful place.

Category: Zemirot (Songs)

Genre: Zemer for the Sabbath

Occasion: Sabbath

Name: אשיר בשירה אל נורא תהלות, Ashir Beshira El Nora Tehillot 

Composer: Avraham ben Yoshiyahu Ha-rofé

Location: Troki, Lithuania

Date: 1636–1687

Acrostic: אברהם חזק “Avraham, be strong!!”

Source: Vilna Siddur, Volume 4, page 102

Visual Representation of Meter:  – – v – – – / – – v – – 

Description of Meter: Each line consists of two half-lines: the first half-line contains two full vowels, followed by a vocal sheva and a full vowel, followed by two more full vowels. The second half-line consists of two full vowels, followed by a vocal sheva and a full vowel, followed by one more full vowel.

Davidson number: א 7934

Karaite origin: Yes

About the author: Abraham ben Yoshiyahu was the son of Yoshiyahu ben Yehuda and the grandson of Yehuda ben Aharon. All three members of this family were prominent Karaite scholars in Troki. Like Zeraḥ ben Natan and Ezra ben Nisan, Abraham’s father, Yoshiyahu, had been one of the correspondents of Yosef Shelomo Delmedigo, and his question about the nature of the human soul was published in Delmedigo’s Sefer Elim.

Abraham was born in 1636, and he was a physician (rofé). He composed several literary works, his favorite topic being medicine and mysticism. Abraham was interested in the Kabbalistic teachings widespread among early modern Jewry. Many of his works survive in manuscripts in East European archives. Abraham was fluent in Latin, and parts of his medical works contain Latin texts. He had at least two sons, Yitsḥaḳ and Yehuda. Abraham died in 1687 at the age of fifty-two.

Sources: Encyclopaedia Judaica; Mann, Texts and Studies; Samuel Fuenn, Keneset Yisra’el (Warsaw, 1886).
